sentences.text: By way of the present petition filed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, the petitioners seek quashing of FIR No.1018/2021 dated 04.12.2021 registered under sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at P.S.: Dabri, New Delhi.

At the outset, it is noticed that Memorandum of Understanding ('MoU') dated 02.01.2024, based upon which the petitioners seeks quashing of the FIR, has been signed only between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2.
The other petitioners are not signatory to the MoU.
The petitioners as well as respondent No.2 are present in court today.
Though respondent No. 2 has signed an affidavit in support of the present petition, she submits that the petitioners are yet to return her dowry articles including jewellery and other articles.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/07/2024 at 01:11:31 Respondent No.2 is not represented by her own counsel.
She says that counsel for the petitioners had assured her that she would get back her dowry articles etc. upon quashing of the present FIR.
In the circumstances, this court is not satisfied that respondent No.2 has consented to the quashing of the FIR unequivocally.
Respondent No.2 seeks time to discuss the matter with petitioner No.1.
